findings.title: KeyError crash when Integration metadata has no sender
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. In build_integration sender is optional (only set if state.get("sender")), so older or webhook-less Integrations have no sender key. A second-org install or reinstall for such an Integration raises KeyError resulting in a 500 instead of the intended error page, blocking legitimate installs.

findings.title: Fresh-install path skips authenticated-user check
findings.body: GitHubInstallation returns pipeline.next_step() immediately when Integration.DoesNotExist for the supplied installation_id, without comparing pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to the installer. An attacker can win the race before the installation webhook creates the Integration, or use an installation_id that has never been seen, and complete the pipeline having only passed OAuth as themselves, defeating the mismatch check described in the PR.

findings.title: Unhandled token-exchange / user-info failures cause 500
findings.body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen for the access_token exchange and get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) with only payload-parsing wrapped in try/except. Network errors, non-200 GitHub responses, or ApiError from get_user_info propagate as 500 instead of rendering the github-integration-failed template. The code only handles missing access_token/login keys, not exceptions from those calls.

findings.title: Unvalidated installation_id used in GitHub API path
findings.body: installation_id is taken from request.GET or pipeline state and bound without validation, then later interpolated into client.get(f"/app/installations/{installation_id}") in get_installation_info. A value containing slashes or path segments lets a caller make the server issue JWT-authenticated GETs to arbitrary /app/ paths on api.github.com, beyond the intended installation lookup.
